title: Apollo 13: The Failure That Became a Rescue
real_world_anchor: Apollo 13 was a real NASA mission where an oxygen tank problem forced the crew and ground teams to improvise a return home.
facts: An oxygen tank problem forced the Moon landing to be aborted.
The crew returned safely after major engineering work from space and the ground.
hook_first_sentence: Apollo 13 became famous because the mission failed at the worst possible time.
script: Apollo 13 became famous because the mission failed at the worst possible time. In April 1970, the crew was on the way to the Moon when an oxygen tank problem changed everything. The landing was over. The new mission was survival. The shocking part is that the rescue was not one heroic button press. It was small engineering decisions, checked again and again, while three people were trapped in space. That is why the story still works for Shorts: the danger is huge, but the solution is human. People on Earth helped bring a broken spacecraft home.
retention_hook: Turns a known mission into a step-by-step rescue.
why_it_worked: Named event, date, stakes, and clear human problem solving.
what_to_improve: Avoid using movie dialogue as fact.

title: The Great Molasses Flood
real_world_anchor: In 1919, a storage tank burst in Boston and released a wave of molasses through city streets.
facts: The disaster happened in Boston in January 1919.
A large molasses tank burst and sent a wave through the area.
The strange material makes the event memorable, but the disaster was deadly and real.
hook_first_sentence: Boston once had a deadly flood made of molasses.
script: Boston once had a deadly flood made of molasses. That sounds like a joke until you hear the date: January 1919. A huge storage tank burst, and thick molasses moved through the street like a dark wave. The shocking detail is how ordinary the setup was. It was not a volcano, a war, or a storm. It was an industrial tank people passed near every day. That is why the fact sticks. History is not always distant and grand. Sometimes it is one weak container, one normal street, and a danger nobody expects until it breaks.
retention_hook: The material is strange, but the framing stays serious.
why_it_worked: A weird real event with a clear cause and visual hook.
what_to_improve: Do not make the tragedy sound funny.

title: The Rosetta Stone: One Object, Three Scripts
real_world_anchor: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars understand Egyptian hieroglyphs because it carried related text in multiple scripts.
facts: The Rosetta Stone is held by the British Museum.
It has text in hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Greek.
The object became central to deciphering Egyptian hieroglyphs.
hook_first_sentence: One broken stone helped unlock a lost writing system.
script: One broken stone helped unlock a lost writing system. The Rosetta Stone is famous because the same message appears in different scripts, including Greek and Egyptian writing. That gave scholars a bridge. The surprising part is that the object does not look like a magic key. It looks like a damaged slab. But history often works that way. A simple object survives, and centuries later people realize it is the missing clue. The lesson for a short is clear: show the object first, then reveal that its value was not beauty. Its value was translation.
retention_hook: A humble object becomes a huge intellectual key.
why_it_worked: Object-first storytelling with a clear payoff.
what_to_improve: Avoid oversimplifying the full decipherment process.

title: The Year Without a Summer
real_world_anchor: The 1815 Mount Tambora eruption affected weather and helped create the 1816 Year Without a Summer.
facts: The eruption affected global climate conditions.
1816 became known as the Year Without a Summer in parts of the world.
hook_first_sentence: One volcano helped make summer disappear.
script: One volcano helped make summer disappear. In 1815, Mount Tambora erupted, and the effects did not stay near the mountain. Ash and gases reached the atmosphere, and the next year brought strange cold weather in many places. The shocking detail is the delay. People far away did not need to see the eruption to feel it. Crops struggled. Seasons felt wrong. That is what makes this history fact powerful: the cause was one island volcano, but the effect reached ordinary dinner tables. Sometimes history travels through the weather before people understand why.
retention_hook: Explains a global effect from one event.
why_it_worked: Clear cause-effect structure and everyday consequences.
what_to_improve: Avoid implying every cold event that year had one simple cause.

title: The Emancipation Proclamation
real_world_anchor: The Emancipation Proclamation was a Civil War document issued by Abraham Lincoln in 1863.
facts: The Emancipation Proclamation took effect on January 1, 1863.
It declared enslaved people in Confederate-held areas to be free.
It changed the purpose and stakes of the Civil War.
hook_first_sentence: One document changed what the Civil War was fighting over.
script: One document changed what the Civil War was fighting over. The Emancipation Proclamation took effect on January 1, 1863. It did not end slavery everywhere in one day, and that detail matters. But it declared enslaved people in Confederate-held areas to be free and changed the meaning of the war. The strong short-video angle is honesty. Do not oversell it as instant freedom for everyone. Show why it mattered: a legal document became a war aim, a public promise, and a step toward a different country.
what_to_improve: Avoid claiming the document ended slavery everywhere.

title: The Underground Railroad Was Not a Train
real_world_anchor: The Underground Railroad was a network of people, places, and routes used by freedom seekers.
facts: The Underground Railroad was not a literal railroad.
It involved people, safe places, routes, and coded language.
Freedom seekers and helpers took serious risks.
hook_first_sentence: The Underground Railroad was not underground, and it was not a train.
script: The Underground Railroad was not underground, and it was not a train. That is the first detail that makes people stop scrolling. It was a real network of routes, helpers, homes, and coded words used by freedom seekers. The danger was not symbolic. A wrong knock, a wrong road, or a person who could not be trusted could change everything. The best way to tell it in a short is with simple images: a dark road, a lamp, a door, a map. The name sounds hidden, but the courage was real.
retention_hook: Starts by correcting the common literal misunderstanding.
why_it_worked: Simple correction plus high-stakes real history.
what_to_improve: Do not compress many different routes into one fake story.
